- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.0) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for next 3–5 periods.
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive downward moves), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to match recent 5-day average trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits short-term sentiment noise; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce volatility amplification.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model delays reaction; forecast should adjust 1–2 periods ahead of sentiment change.
